Visual deficiencies in young children can result in strabismus (crossed eyes), amblyopia (lazy eye) or focusing difficulties, and adults and seniors need to be tested for cataracts, glaucoma, macular degeneration, retinal detachment and several other conditions we assess in our routine examination. Many visual problems can be corrected with glasses, contact lenses, or laser vision correction. Whether you want a spectacular new look with one of our designer frames or designer sunglasses, or the latest innovations in contact lens technology, our experienced and knowledgeable eye team will be there for your personalized fitting.

service.name: Eye Exams
service.summary: A full eye examination that checks your prescription and the health of your eyes.
service.description: A friendly staff member will start the exam with a computerized automated refraction and eye pressure testing. You will then see the doctor for your examination. The exam will start off with a thorough history of your previous eye exams, medications and family medical history. The doctor will then check your eyeglass prescription for distance and near/computer vision. A detailed ocular health assessment follows, where cataracts, glaucoma, retinal disease and a host of other conditions are evaluated. Pupillary dilation may be required. The doctor will then summarize the results and provide a written prescription. Your optometrist can also prescribe medications to treat eye infections and other eye conditions. We have digital retinal imaging to monitor your retina for diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and macular degeneration, and we perform MTO (Ministry of Transport) vision assessments and Esterman visual field testing.

service.name: Adult & Senior Eye Exams
service.summary: Annual comprehensive exams for adults and seniors, including screening for cataracts, glaucoma and macular degeneration.
service.description: Annual eye exams are recommended for adults and seniors. A comprehensive eye exam not only tests your eyeglass prescription but also tests for a variety of common ocular health conditions and disease. Conditions such as cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and macular degeneration are just a few that can be detected only through a comprehensive eye examination. A friendly staff member will start the exam with computerized automated refraction and eye pressure testing. You will then see the doctor, who begins with a thorough history of your previous eye exams, medications, and family medical history, then checks your eyeglass prescription for distance and near/computer vision. A detailed ocular health assessment follows, where cataracts, glaucoma, retinal disease and a host of other conditions are evaluated. Pupillary dilation may be required, and advanced testing such as Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), retinal photos and visual field testing may be recommended. The doctor will then summarize the results and provide a written prescription.

service.name: Children’s Eye Exams
service.summary: Gentle, thorough eye exams for babies, pre-schoolers and school-age children.
service.description: Annual eye exams are recommended for children under the age of 19. Babies are recommended to have their first exam at 6 months, with annual exams after that. It is especially important that children have their pre-school eye exam at 4 to 5 years of age. There are several eye conditions that must be evaluated in childhood: conditions such as strabismus (crossed eyes or eye turns) and amblyopia (lazy eye) must be detected and treated early to ensure proper visual development. A child’s exam starts with an auto-refraction to measure their prescription. The doctor then tests visual acuity, fine tunes the prescription, and checks into ocular health. In addition to the usual health checks, pupillary reflex testing, stereo-vision, cover test, extraocular movement, and colour vision testing are an important part of a child’s eye exam.
service.audience: Children under 19, from 6 months of age

service.name: MTO and Police Eye Exams
service.summary: Occupational vision testing and paperwork for driving, policing and other job requirements.
service.description: We perform all the tests necessary to fill out your application for Police, RCMP, Ministry of Transportation, or other occupational eye exams. We have colour vision testing, stereo vision testing as well as peripheral vision testing.
service.audience: Police, RCMP, Ministry of Transportation and other occupational applicants

service.name: Contact Lens Fitting
service.summary: Fitting, training and free trial lenses for new and experienced contact lens wearers.
service.description: Advances in contact lens technology have made them much healthier to wear. Newer silicone-hydrogel materials allow more oxygen through the lens, allowing your eyes to breathe, which reduces signs of corneal hypoxia. One-day disposable lenses reduce eye infections as compared to reusable lenses. New contact lens wearers first get a comprehensive eye exam, followed by a discussion on the suitability of contact lenses. Candidates then go through a training process where they are shown how to insert and remove lenses, and lenses are checked for excellent fit and vision. An optometrist or optician will ensure an optimal lens fitting for maximal comfort and ocular health. New wearers are sent home with a set of free trial lenses to test out in their normal daily routine; once satisfied, the lenses can be purchased at our office. We carry all the major brands as well as custom order lenses, there is no charge for exchanges of unused boxes, no charge for follow-up visits for problems related to lenses purchased at our office, big savings with manufacturer rebate offers, and convenient direct shipping to your home.

service.name: Dry Eye Testing
service.summary: Diagnostic testing for dry eye disease, with IPL and radiofrequency treatment in the clinic.
service.description: Do your eyes feel sandy or gritty? Or do they water for no particular reason? If so you may have dry eye disease. Dry eye disease occurs when your tear quality or quantity is abnormal. We have specialized diagnostic tests, as well as state of the art treatment for dry eye disease. Dry eye diagnostic testing with the IDRA includes meibography, tear film analysis and blepharitis assessment. Intense Pulsed Light (IPL) has been shown to relieve dry eye symptoms through its thermal action, by melting away thick oil clogging up the meibomian glands; IPL also shrinks the fine blood vessels on the lid margin that carry inflammatory factors, and helps reduce sun damage, fine lines and wrinkles by boosting production of skin firming proteins like collagen and elastin. During IPL treatment the pulses may cause a snapping sensation and warmth; following your treatment brown spots will darken and skin may appear red for up to 24 hours, and your improved complexion should be visible three weeks post treatment. Best results typically require 4-5 treatments spaced one month apart. The Radio Frequency (RF) procedure generates heat at an optimal temperature within the eyelid tissue, melting the oil that is clogging the glands so it can be expressed easily; as a bonus, RF reduces skin laxity and promotes collagen growth, resulting in wrinkle reduction.

service.name: BlephEx Treatment
service.summary: A painless in-office eyelid cleaning that clears the bacteria and debris behind blepharitis.
service.description: Do you frequently experience red irritated eyes, a sandy or gritty feeling and flaky material on your lids and eyelashes? This is likely due to an overgrowth of bacteria on your eyelids. Symptoms of blepharitis include burning, itching, watery eyes and crusty eyelids. If left untreated, blepharitis can result in dry eyes, infections and the formation of styes. BlephEx™ is a tool that painlessly removes eyelid debris and the bacteria that grow in this debris. It uses a microsponge and medical detergent to gently cleanse your eyelids. BlephEx™ may need to be performed every 6 months to maintain eyelid health.

service.name: OCT Testing
service.summary: Non-invasive scanning that shows the detailed layers of your retina and optic nerve.
service.description: Optical Coherence Tomography is an advanced non-invasive imaging test. This test allows your optometrist to visualize detailed layers of your retina and optic nerve. It allows for early detection of conditions such as glaucoma, macula degeneration, and diabetic eye disease. This testing service is offered in our office and is recommended for all adults and seniors.
service.audience: Recommended for all adults and seniors

service.name: Management of Eye Disease
service.summary: Monitoring and care for diabetic eye disease, glaucoma, macular degeneration and cataracts.
service.description: Diabetes can affect various organs in your body, including your eyes. Fluctuating blood sugar can weaken the blood vessels in your retina, causing them to leak, and retinal bleeding can damage its structure, causing loss of vision. A diabetic eye exam includes a dilated retinal exam, where the doctor inserts drops to dilate your pupils; after waiting 15 minutes, the retina is examined for signs of diabetic retinopathy, and an OCT test is recommended to provide a more thorough examination. Glaucoma is a disease of the optic nerve, which slowly deteriorates, typically over several years, resulting in the gradual loss of peripheral vision; untreated glaucoma can result in complete vision loss. Macula degeneration is a result of the disruption of the area of the retina which provides central vision; the two varieties are dry macula degeneration (slowly progressing) and wet macula degeneration (potentially rapidly progressing), and it can be inherited. Cataracts are a result of the clouding of the crystalline lens within the eye, so vision gradually becomes cloudy and acuity decreases; cataracts typically worsen with age and can be accelerated by conditions such as diabetes, but cataract surgery is quick and very successful in restoring vision.

service.name: Laser Vision Correction
service.summary: Consultations that work out whether laser surgery suits your eyes, and which procedure fits.
service.description: Laser vision correction is a great solution for those of you frustrated with glasses or contact lenses. Laser surgery corrects those who are near-sighted, far-sighted or who have astigmatism, and there are procedures to correct presbyopia so one does not need reading glasses. There are several types of vision correction surgeries available, and you may be a good candidate for one procedure but not so great for another. Every consultation starts with a comprehensive eye exam, including a detailed history, visual needs questionnaire, measurement of eyeglass prescription and evaluation of ocular health. Through this process we can determine the most suitable laser vision correction for you. Call us to schedule your consultation today.

service.name: Computer Related Eye Strain
service.summary: Advice and office lenses for the headaches and dry eyes that come with screen work.
service.description: We are all spending more and more time on computers, smart phones, tablets and other devices, and this adds a lot more strain on the visual system. Our eyes are relaxed when looking at a distance, but more stressed when focusing up close, so being on a computer device for hours a day adds to eye strain and fatigue. Our blink rate also decreases when focusing on our work. Headache and dry eye are a direct result of computer related eye strain. The 20-20-20 rule is a good habit for heavy computer users: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet or further (out a window or into the distance) for a period of 20 seconds. This practice allows our eyes to reset after staring and helps reduce computer related eye strain. We have several products, such as office lenses, to help combat computer related eye strain. Call us to schedule your consultation today.

faq.question: How often should I have an eye exam?
faq.answer: Most adults should have an eye exam every 1 to 2 years. If you have vision problems, a family history of eye disease, or certain health conditions like diabetes, more frequent exams may be recommended by your optometrist.

faq.question: How long does an eye exam take?
faq.answer: A standard eye exam usually takes about 30 to 60 minutes, depending on the complexity of the tests and whether you require additional evaluations, such as for contact lenses or eye conditions.

faq.question: What do I need to bring with me for an eye exam?
faq.answer: Please bring your current eyeglasses or contact lenses, a list of medications you are taking, your health card or insurance information, and any questions or concerns you have about your vision or eye health.

faq.question: Why is an eye test important?
faq.answer: Eye tests are essential not only for detecting changes in your vision but also for identifying early signs of eye conditions and systemic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol.

faq.question: Why do I need more frequent eye tests if I’m diabetic?
faq.answer: Diabetes increases the risk of diabetic retinopathy and other eye complications. Regular eye exams help monitor changes and allow for early intervention to prevent vision loss.

faq.question: Do I still need glasses if I get contact lenses?
faq.answer: Yes, it is recommended to have a backup pair of glasses even if you wear contact lenses regularly. Glasses give your eyes a break from contacts and are useful in case of irritation or emergencies.

faq.question: When should my child have their first eye exam?
faq.answer: Children should have their first comprehensive eye exam between 6 and 9 months of age, another at 2 to 5 years old, and annually once they start school. Early detection is key to ensuring healthy visual development.

faq.question: What does a comprehensive eye examination include?
faq.answer: A comprehensive exam evaluates vision sharpness, eye muscle function, pupil response, side vision, eye pressure, and the overall health of the eye using specialized equipment.

faq.question: Do I need to wear my contact lenses to my contact lens appointment?
faq.answer: Yes, wearing your contact lenses to the appointment helps the optometrist assess the fit, comfort, and effectiveness of your lenses. Be sure to bring your lens case and solution as well.

faq.question: What are the common signs of eye problems that I should watch out for?
faq.answer: Watch for symptoms like blurry vision, headache, eye pain, redness, flashes of light, floaters, double vision, or sudden vision loss. Seek prompt evaluation if any of these occur.

faq.question: How can I reduce eye strain, especially when working on a computer?
faq.answer: Follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Adjust screen brightness, reduce glare, and ensure proper lighting and ergonomics.

faq.question: What are the risk factors for conditions such as glaucoma, cataracts, and macular degeneration, and how can I lower my risk?
faq.answer: Risk factors include age, family history, smoking, UV exposure, and certain health conditions. Protect your eyes with sunglasses, eat a balanced diet rich in antioxidants, avoid smoking, and schedule regular eye exams for early detection.
